entities.name: Johan Verstolk van Soelen
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Johan Gijsbert Verstolk van Soelen (1776–1845) stands as a pivotal figure in the diplomatic landscape of the nascent Kingdom of the Netherlands, serving as its Minister of Foreign Affairs for an uninterrupted sixteen years, from 1825 to 1841. His tenure, spanning the reigns of King William I and the early years of William II, was defined by the profound geopolitical challenges following the Napoleonic Wars and, most critically, the seismic upheaval of the Belgian Revolution. As a statesman, Verstolk was instrumental in attempting to preserve the territorial integrity of the United Kingdom of the Netherlands and later, in managing the complex international negotiations that ultimately led to the formal separation of Belgium.

Verstolk began his career in the diplomatic service, acting as the Dutch envoy to the United States from 1801 to 1803, before a period of private life during the French occupation. Following the restoration of Dutch independence, he returned to public service, eventually ascending to the foreign ministry. His most significant test arrived in 1830 with the outbreak of the Belgian Revolution. Verstolk tenaciously defended the Dutch position during the London Conference of 1830-1839, a protracted series of negotiations involving the Great Powers (Britain, France, Prussia, Austria, and Russia). He steadfastly advocated for the retention of Luxembourg and Limburg, and for favorable terms regarding the navigation of the Scheldt River and the division of the national debt, often acting as the King's principal advisor in these intricate diplomatic maneuvers.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Johan Verstolk van Soelen's steadfast diplomacy during the Belgian Revolution profoundly shaped the territorial boundaries of the modern Netherlands and Belgium, securing key regions like Limburg for the Dutch state. His efforts averted further destabilization in Europe and defined the young nation's international posture for decades.
